name: 2021 Prairie Avenue — the Adams/High house, brick under a steep front gable with a round corner turret (T-3633)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½B brick dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: Refined in place from the district draft (T-2352) onto the K01 frontage assembly by T-3633, piece 1 of T-1917 (package S08 of the T-1837 programme): the house's plan off the 1911 sheet 35 trace (the main body, the round of its north-west corner and the projection on its south flank, the '2B' and '1B' rear ranges), and its steep front gable, round corner turret over an arched porch, gabled south wing, tall stack and slate roofs off the one photograph of it, Chicagology's undated halftone captioned 'Shirley T. High Residence'. The Daily News of 19 January 1940 (cited in the 1973 Commission report) calls it a 2½-storey, 16-room house built in the late 1870s by Benjamin Adams and sold in 1886 to James L. High, Shirley T. High's father; the photograph's Queen Anne form may be High's of 1886-1887 rather than Adams's, so the picture is evidence of its own date and the record claims the 1904 target only through the 1911 sheet, which draws the same plan. Liberty L-k01-2021-high-3633.

documented_range.note: Drawn on the 1911 sheet, which the T-1842 census rules present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), with the plan the photograph shows (the rounded north-west corner, the projection on the south flank). The photograph is undated; the record claims the 1904 target to the sheet's date and no more.

position.symbolic_location: 2021 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2021 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The corner of the front block's rear line on the main body's north flank (10.5 m behind the rear wall the draft stood on, where the south wing stands out from the south flank), read off the traced 1911 sheet 35 outline (s35fp-2021-b1, data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. The draft's corner stood 10.5 m further back and 1.2 m south: it took the largest rectangle inside the trace, which left out the main body's north 1.2 m. Rotation 179.389 degrees (the draft's) turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body the 1911 sheet draws, '2½B', read off the traced outline in this frame: its front 18.3 m from its rear wall and its two flanks 9.25 m apart. The trace's round of the north-west corner (about 1.3 m before the front) is the turret, and its projection on the south flank (u 5.3-10.5 m, 4.15 m out) the south wing, both built as bays; the trace's small cut at the front's south corner (about a metre) is not built (the photograph shows the corner square).

stories.note: '2½B' printed on the 1911 sheet over the house: two full storeys and a half storey in the roof, the half storey the attic under the front gable, whose three lights the photograph shows.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the house brick, and the photograph shows brick walls from the base course to the gable's head, the turret included.

principal_floor_m.note: The porch's floor and the front's base course read off the photograph through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): both at about y 1430 px, 2.2 m over the yard's grade; the stoop climbs to it in about eleven risers.

storey_heights_m.note: Read off the photograph through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): the string course under the second-floor lights at about 5.9 m, the second-floor lights from 6.25 to 8.45 m and the eave over the south flank at 9.8-9.9 m (y 610 px at the front corner, 730 px at the side wing), so 2.2 + 3.8 + 3.8 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick front three bricks thick, the contract's ordinary masonry front. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A 13 in brick side wall, the contract's ordinary. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

eave_overhang_m.note: The slate overhangs the south flank by about a foot in the photograph (y 600-620 px over the wall's head).

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing before the porch's mouth, the contract's ordinary. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

service_wall_brick.note: The rear and north walls no picture shows, in the contract's common brick. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

face_brick.note: The photograph shows one dark brick on the front, the turret and the south flank alike (a coarse halftone: monochrome, so the red is RECONSTRUCTED, as every pressed brick front on the avenue's K01 houses).

street_front_trim.note: Plain stone heads over the street lights: the halftone shows the heads as pale bands and no carved hood. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

wall_head.note: No cornice across the front: the front wall runs up into its gable, and the flanks end at a plain slate eave (the photograph).

roof_form.note: The main roof runs back from the street under one ridge in the photograph, its south slope seen whole from the front's gable to the tall stack: built as K01's hip over the long, narrow block, its street end hidden behind the front's gable (shaped_gable), so its two long slopes are the photograph's.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The front gable's apex at about 15.5 m over grade (y 70 px, x 545 px, through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json)) over an eave at 9.8 m and a front 9.25 m across: a rise of 5.7 m in 4.6 m, 51 degrees at the gable; the slopes behind it are laid at 49 degrees, so the gable's head stands the kit's 0.3 m (here 0.38 m) over the ridge, as a coped wall gable must (within tolerance: about 0.2 m at the ridge).

roof_covering.note: The photograph shows slate on every roof, the turret's cone among them, snow lying on it.

shaped_gable.note: The steep front gable the register names: the front wall carried up over its whole width to an apex at 15.5 m (see roof_pitch_deg), its raking edges straight, with three attic lights from 9.85 to 11.5 m read off the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json) (x 445-500, 535-590 and 628-688 px, about 0.6 m each, the left two paired), their centres 0.5 m north and 0.6 and 1.7 m south of the front's middle. The photograph's slate runs a little past the rakes; K01's wall gable carries a coping there instead (within tolerance, recorded in the match record). A finial stands on the apex (T-3634): a knob on a slender turned neck, its foot spreading onto the rakes, from the apex at about y 75 px up to y 30 px, about 0.45 m tall and 0.16 m across through the solved camera; built as K01's turned spike at that size (its turning is the kit's, the halftone giving only its outline).

stoop_width_m.note: The flight is seen climbing along the front from the north under snow; its width is set to the arch's 1.8 m opening and its cheeks. The photograph's flight climbs along the front from the north; K01's stoop runs straight out from the door (recorded in the match record). (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

entrance_bay.note: The arched porch at the front's north end, under the turret (K01's south is the low-v end, the house's north).

front_bays.note: Two bays on the front, read off the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): the porch's arched mouth at x 235-420 px (v 1.2-3.5 m), its centre 2.35 m from the front's north end, under the turret; and the broad lights of both storeys at x 690-820 px (v 6.7-8.1 m).

side_bays.note: The front block's north flank, which no picture shows: two bays of the kit's sash, the front one level with the south flank's light. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

north_bays.note: The south flank's one narrow light a storey, 1.4 m behind the front corner (x 965-1005 px through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json)); the rest of the flank to the wing is blank in the photograph.

rear_bays.note: No picture sees the rear wall; the kit's ordinary bays. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

sash_by_storey.note: The front's lights read off the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): on the principal floor from 2.3 to 4.75 m (y 1155-1420 px, about 1.3 m wide, built at the contract's widest 1.15 m), on the second floor from 6.25 to 8.45 m (y 755-990 px, about 1.1 m wide).

0.head: plain
0.why_not_ordinary: the narrow light between the porch's arch and the broad window, x 505-560 px and y 1425-1150 px on the photograph's solved camera (v 4.53-5.18 m, 2.30-4.98 m over grade): one light 0.65 m across, its sill on the broad light's and its head level with it, no pale head over it

front_bays_by_storey.note: The second floor's lights read off the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): the light beside the turret (x 410-505 px, v 3.4-4.5 m) and the broad light over the principal floor's (x 700-810 px); over the porch the turret takes the storey. T-3634: the principal storey keeps the porch's and the broad light's bays and takes one light read off the same camera between them: a dark narrow opening at x 505-560 px (v 4.53-5.18 m, so 0.65 m across, centre 4.86 m) whose foot stands on the base course's snow line at y 1425 px (2.30 m, the broad light's sill) and whose top reaches y 1150 px (4.98 m), level with the broad light's head at y 1160 px; a paler band across it at y 1230-1280 px (3.7-4.2 m) is read as its meeting rails or a blind, not as two openings, since the broad light beside it carries its transom bar at the same height. Its head is plain: the halftone shows no pale hood over it.

basement_lights.note: The basement's lights under the front's broad window and the flank's narrow one, dark openings at about 0.4-1.2 m over the snow (x 665-825 px, y 1530-1620 px, through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json)).

street_front_round_heads.note: The porch's mouth cut round-headed in the brick front (T-3283's brick door arch): the photograph's arch at x 235-420 px; every street light is square-headed, so no storey's lights are rounded.

window_kit.note: The kit's two-over-two sash; the halftone shows blinds drawn in most lights and no muntins.

entrance_kit.note: The round-arched porch the register names: in the photograph a broad round arch at x 235-420 px (v 1.2-3.5 m), its crown at about 4.75 m over grade and its opening about 1.8 m wide, opening on a porch with a small light in its north wall and the door at its south end. Built as the kit's round-headed principal entrance cut in the brick front (street_front_round_heads.door) in a 0.45 m reveal: K01 builds an open porch behind an arch (its loggia) only behind a stone front's voussoirs, so the porch's depth, its small north light and its door at the south end are not built, and the match record says so.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the turret's one second-floor light in the photograph (x 200-285 px, y 820-1000 px), from about 6.25 to 8.0 m

bays.note: The turret, read off the photograph and the 1911 sheet: the round corner turret the register names stands at the front's north corner over the porch, its body from the second floor (the ledge over the porch at y 1000-1060 px) to the main eave (y 690 px, 9.8 m) and a slate cone to about 14.2 m (y 245 px) under a finial: the cone's top sheathed in a pale metal cap that flares to a lip about 0.5 m across (y 255-330 px) under a short dark knob, built as K08's turned finial on a plain collar 0.2 m out (the kit's least; its fall, at the cone's pitch, 0.6 m) laid in zinc (the metal is reconstructed: the halftone shows only that it is pale; T-3634); the sheet draws its round about 1.3 m before the front (traced part, 2.8 m across). Built as a round K08 oriel on a rounded apron (its foot 0.5 m under the second floor, where the photograph's ledge runs over the porch) over the porch's mouth, a half round 2.4 m across and 1.2 m out (the kit's deepest round oriel, a half round so its cone closes against the roof; the trace's round is about 2.8 m across, within about 0.2 m a side).

chimneys.note: Two of the photograph's three stacks, placed through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): the tall one on the south flank about 5 m behind the front (x 1090-1210 px, its top at about 16.5 m, y 25 px), and one over the north wall behind the turret (x 400-440 px). The third, on the ridge about 11 m back (x 1010-1080 px), stands over the body behind the front block, the south wing, and is built as that wing's stack (rear_wings, T-3634).

rainwater.note: The photograph shows one downpipe, on the south flank where it meets the wing (x 1270-1280 px), from the eave to the ground; K01 hangs a side wall's pipe only by its rear corner, so the pipes stand there (the one the photograph shows is within tolerance in place: about 10 m back along the flank).

boundary.note: RECONSTRUCTED as a whole because the fence's run past the print is invented; what is read off the photograph through its solved camera (T-3634) is this. The street front is open: no fence, wall or coping stands before the front, the stoop's flight or the basement lights (x 0-1300 px, the snow running to the walk), so nothing is laid across it and the K14 walk comes out to the public walk. A low fence of pointed white pickets on two rails between square posts stands before the south wing (x 1325-1826 px, its first post at x 1325): its top line rises toward the horizon as it runs right (y 1630 px at its first post, about 1610 at x 1600), which a run along the south lot line receding from the street draws and a run along the street does not (that would fall as it nears the camera), so it is laid on the lot line, s 14.85, from X 11.3 m (where the camera's ray through its first post meets the line, 3.35 m short of the street line) back. Its height, 0.9 m, is the pickets' read against the basement's 0.8 m lights at a like distance; its foot is below the print's edge. INVENTED: its run past the print's right edge, carried to the south wing's rear corner (X -5.2 m), and the pale paint's colour (the picture is monochrome). (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

yard.note: The walk to the stoop in stone flags, as the avenue's other K01 fronts; the photograph's yard is under snow. (L-k01-2021-high-3633)

rear_wings.note: Everything the 1911 sheet draws behind the front block, as K01 wings (traced parts s35fp-2021-b1 p2-p3). THE SOUTH WING: the broad side wing with a secondary gable the register names, the sheet's projection on the south flank 7.8 m behind the front, 5.2 m along the flank and 4.15 m out, seen in the photograph from x 1287 px to the picture's edge through the photograph's solved camera (data/reference_views/high_house_2021_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): a light a storey in its west face (a low broad light of small panes at 3.35-4.25 m, then 6.25-8.35 m and 9.8-10.9 m, built in the wing's one row of sizes a storey, so its lowest light is 2.8-4.3 m and its top light 9.15-10.65 m: each within about half a metre), its eave at 11.0 m (y 590 px) and its slate gable facing south to an apex at about 14.6 m (y 290 px), 54 degrees over its 2.6 m half-width; the light at its south-west corner (x 1610-1700 px) is set in its south face, since the sheet's cut corner there (about a metre) is not built. THE BODY BEHIND IT, 5.4 m to the rear wall and 11.2 m across, two storeys under a slate hip continuing the front's 49 degrees, its lights RECONSTRUCTED. THE '2B' AND '1B' RANGES behind that: the two-storey range 4.1 m deep and the one-storey range 3.6 m behind it, a little narrower, their floors, flat roofs and lights RECONSTRUCTED: no picture sees them. THE THIRD STACK: the photograph's short stack on the ridge about 10.4 m behind the front (x 1010-1090 px, its cap at about y 310 px), placed through the solved camera on the south wing's ridge 5.0 m south of the north flank, 0.8 x 0.7 m in plan (narrower than the front's stacks in the print), its top at 15.6 m, about a metre over the 14.6 m ridge; from this camera its south half stands behind the tall south stack, as the photograph's meets that stack's edge (T-3634).
